local.title: Flat lawns on ground that **drains slowly.**
local.intro: Most lawns in Flint Township sit in neighborhoods built from the 1950s through the 1970s, on flat, heavy soil that drains slowly. They come in thick in spring and stay soft longer than people expect, so the mowing is timed around wet ground.

points.title: Soft ground after the thaw
points.body: After snowmelt and spring rain, low spots in heavy soil hold water. A heavy mower on wet ground leaves ruts that harden into bumps you feel all summer, so on soft days those spots get trimmed instead of driven over.

points.title: Grass grown over the concrete
points.body: On older lawns, grass along the drive and the walk has often crept well onto the concrete. We cut it back to a straight line once, then keep it there every week.

points.title: Where the clippings go
points.body: Grass clippings cannot be burned in the township, and Emterra does not take contractor material. Normal clippings go back into the lawn, which feeds it. Heavy ones after a rainy week go in our trailer.

points.title: Fast growth in May
points.body: MSU Extension notes spring growth can call for a cut every four or five days. Skip a week in May on a thick township lawn and the next cut takes off far more than a third of the blade, which stresses the grass.

logistics.title: How a Flint Township lawn gets mowed.
body: Rob walks the lawn with you, notes the soft spots, the fences and the beds, and gives you a weekly price. Then the crew comes on a set weekday from spring into fall.
Each visit: mowed, string trimmed along the house, fences and beds, edged along the drive, walk and curb, and blown clean. The pattern is your call: straight, curved, crosscut or checkerboard.
Height moves with the season. MSU Extension's general range for Michigan lawns is about 2.5 to 3.5 inches, and staying on the taller side in the heat of summer shades the soil and holds moisture.

facts.label: Clippings
facts.value: Mowed back in, or hauled away

faq.q: Do you mow lawns in Flint Township?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes mows lawns in Flint Township weekly from spring into fall: mowed, trimmed, edged and blown off on a set day. The estimate is free, and our shop in Grand Blanc is about 20 minutes away.

faq.q: Why does my lawn stay soggy in the spring?
faq.a: Usually it is the soil. Most of Flint Township sits on heavy soil that drains slowly, and the low spots drain even worse. Water sits longer in spring and after big rains, and wet ground ruts easily, so we work around the softest spots.

faq.q: How high should I mow my lawn?
faq.a: About 2.5 to 3.5 inches is MSU Extension's general range for Michigan lawns, taking no more than a third of the blade per cut. Mowing on the high side in summer helps shade the soil and hold moisture.

Usually not. Normal clippings go back into the lawn, which is what they are for. When the grass gets ahead of us after a rainy week, we bag it and haul it, since burning clippings is not allowed here and the township hauler does not take contractor material.

faq.q: Can you also take care of the shrubs and beds?
faq.a: Yes, as their own jobs. See [shrub trimming in Flint Township](/shrub-trimming-flint-township-mi/) for hedges and foundation shrubs, and [spring cleanups](/spring-cleanup-flint-township-mi/) for getting the yard ready for the first cut. Edging along the walks and drive is already part of every mowing visit.
